questions.statement: Which word in English refers to a long, thin object you use to write on paper?
questions.context: A student in Barranquilla enters her English classroom and points at objects on her desk.

options.text: Pencil.
options.feedback: A pencil is a long, thin writing tool used on paper.

options.text: Eraser.
options.feedback: An eraser is used to remove pencil marks, not to write.

options.text: Backpack.
options.feedback: A backpack is used to carry objects, not to write on paper.

options.text: Globe.
options.feedback: A globe is a model of the Earth used to study geography.

questions.explanation: Identifying basic classroom objects by their function in English (pencil, eraser, backpack, globe).
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Where are the laptop, the book, and the cup of coffee?
questions.context: Read: "On the teacher's desk there is a laptop, a book, and a cup of coffee."

options.text: On the teacher's desk.
options.feedback: The text clearly states that the objects are on the teacher's desk.

options.text: Under the students' chairs.
options.feedback: The text does not mention chairs or placing objects under them.

options.text: Inside the school cafeteria.
options.feedback: The cafeteria is not mentioned; the location is the teacher's desk.

options.text: On the playground outside.
options.feedback: The text locates the objects in the classroom, not outside.

questions.explanation: Locating classroom objects using the preposition "on" to describe position in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly follows the teacher's instructions?
questions.context: A teacher says: "Open your notebooks at page 10. Take out your pencil and your ruler."

options.text: The students open their notebooks and take out their pencils and rulers.
options.feedback: The verb forms agree with the plural subject "the students".

options.text: The students opens their notebooks and take out their pencils.
options.feedback: "Opens" is singular and does not agree with the plural subject "students".

options.text: The student open their notebooks and takes out their pencils.
options.feedback: The singular subject "student" requires "opens" and "takes", not the plural forms.

options.text: The students opening their notebooks at page ten.
options.feedback: "Opening" is a gerund and needs an auxiliary verb in this context.

questions.explanation: Applying subject-verb agreement with plural classroom subjects in the Simple Present tense.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which preposition best describes the position of the dictionary?
questions.context: A student in Ibague organizes her desk: "The dictionary is next to the notebook. The pencil case is under the chair."

options.text: Next to.
options.feedback: "Next to" indicates that the dictionary is beside the notebook.

options.text: Under.
options.feedback: "Under" describes something below another object, not beside it.

options.text: Between.
options.feedback: "Between" requires two reference objects on each side.

options.text: Behind.
options.feedback: "Behind" describes something at the back of another object.

questions.explanation: Using basic prepositions of place (next to, under, between, behind) in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct request using "there is / there are".
questions.context: A student must borrow an item and says: "Excuse me, teacher, may I borrow a ruler? I do not have one in my pencil case."

options.text: There are some rulers on the teacher's desk.
options.feedback: "There are" agrees with the plural noun "rulers".

options.text: There is some rulers on the teacher's desk.
options.feedback: "There is" is used with singular nouns, not with the plural "rulers".

options.text: There are a ruler on the teacher's desk.
options.feedback: "A ruler" is singular and requires "there is", not "there are".

options.text: There is some ruler on the teacher's desks.
options.feedback: "Desks" is plural and should be preceded by "there are", not "there is".

questions.explanation: Applying subject-verb agreement between "there is" and "there are" with classroom object nouns.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Where is the dictionary in relation to the English book?
questions.context: Read: "The math book is in the backpack. The English book is on the table. The dictionary is next to the English book."

options.text: It is right beside the English book.
options.feedback: "Next to" means the dictionary is beside the English book.

options.text: It is inside the backpack with the math book.
options.feedback: The text locates the math book in the backpack, not the dictionary.

options.text: It is under the English book.
options.feedback: The text says "next to", not "under", so the dictionary is not below.

options.text: It is on a different floor in the school.
options.feedback: Both objects are described in the same classroom context.

questions.explanation: Analyzing spatial relationships between classroom objects described in English text.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which inference about the student's school supplies is correct?
questions.context: Two students talk: "I have five notebooks, three pencils, and one ruler in my backpack."

options.text: The student has more notebooks than pencils.
options.feedback: Five notebooks is greater than three pencils, so the inference is correct.

options.text: The student has the same number of notebooks and pencils.
options.feedback: The numbers are different: 5 notebooks vs 3 pencils.

options.text: The student has more pencils than notebooks.
options.feedback: Three pencils is less than five notebooks, so this inference is wrong.

options.text: The student has no rulers at all.
options.feedback: The text clearly states the student has one ruler.

questions.explanation: Drawing correct inferences about quantities of classroom objects from a short English description.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the author's main message about caring for classroom objects?
questions.context: Read: 'Taking care of classroom objects is important. When students return pencils, close notebooks, and clean the board, the classroom stays organized and ready for everyone.'

options.text: Students should take care of classroom objects to keep the room organized for everyone.
options.feedback: The text links responsibility for supplies with a better shared learning space.

options.text: Only the teacher should take care of classroom objects.
options.feedback: The text speaks about "students" returning and organizing items, not only the teacher.

options.text: It is fine to leave pencils on the floor after class.
options.feedback: The text promotes returning pencils, the opposite of leaving them on the floor.

options.text: Cleaning the board is unnecessary in a classroom.
options.feedback: Cleaning the board is listed as a positive example of taking care.

questions.explanation: Evaluating the main message of a short persuasive paragraph about responsibility for classroom objects.
questions.subject: ingles
